title: Splunk search and dispatch error signals
description: Patterns for Splunk search-peer failures, search timeouts, and dispatch or licensing errors in Splunkd and search-head logs.

patterns.name: search peer failure
patterns.explanation: Splunk could not use a search peer because it failed, went down, or became unavailable.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because distributed search coverage is impaired at the peer boundary.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Planned peer rotation, rolling restarts, and network maintenance can be transient.

patterns.name: search timeout
patterns.explanation: A Splunk search did not complete before its timeout.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because the query failed to finish, while the service may still be healthy.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Large exploratory searches and intentionally short test timeouts can trigger this signal.

patterns.name: search bundle initialization error
patterns.explanation: Splunk could not initialize the search bundle needed to execute a search.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because search dispatch cannot begin with an unavailable bundle.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: A bundle deployment race or intentionally invalid test bundle can cause this error.

patterns.name: license violation
patterns.explanation: Splunk reported a license policy violation.
patterns.severityRationale: Notice because the event needs operational review but is not a clean/infected verdict.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Evaluation environments and planned license-boundary tests can emit this event.
